results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if the page/row identifier is unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Locate the task by title using NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE_WITH_FILTER (paginate with has_more/next_cursor; if multiple matches, select the exact one).

[Optional (if property keys/types or allowed options are uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Confirm the database schema using NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE (identify the status-like property type and valid option names).
[Optional (to confirm the target before writing)] [Prerequisite]: Read the task using NOTION_FETCH_ROW (capture current status and confirm the correct page for commenting).
[Required] [Step]: Update the task status using NOTION_UPDATE_ROW_DATABASE (send a schema-valid status/select payload and verify returned properties).

[Fallback (if NOTION_UPDATE_ROW_DATABASE returns HTTP 400 validation errors)] [Fallback]: Retry the same property change using NOTION_UPDATE_PAGE (use correctly typed property objects and exact option labels).
[Required] [Step]: Add a comment using NOTION_CREATE_COMMENT (attach to the task page as parent and send a rich_text body).
[Optional (for verification after writes)] [Next Step]: Re-read using NOTION_FETCH_ROW (if values look stale immediately after update, fetch once more).
[Optional (if task identifier is missing/ambiguous)] [Prerequisite]: Locate the task using CLICKUP_GET_TASKS (page through results until completion, then select the exact match before writing).
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Retrieve current task details using CLICKUP_GET_TASK (confirm correct item; capture its list identifier and current status).
[Optional (if status label is unvalidated or an update fails)] [Prerequisite]: Retrieve list details using CLICKUP_GET_LIST (confirm the exact allowed status label for that list).
[Required] [Step]: Request confirmation if moving to a terminal/closed state, then update the task using CLICKUP_UPDATE_TASK (set status to an allowed exact value; change only intended fields).
[Required] [Next Step]: After a successful update, add a progress/audit note using CLICKUP_CREATE_TASK_COMMENT (provide required inputs; store returned comment identifier for potential edits).
[Optional (for verification)] [Next Step]: Re-fetch using CLICKUP_GET_TASK and/or CLICKUP_GET_TASK_COMMENTS (confirm final status and that the comment is visible).
[Optional (if the posted comment needs correction)] [Fallback]: Edit the comment using CLICKUP_UPDATE_COMMENT (use the saved comment identifier or find it via CLICKUP_GET_TASK_COMMENTS).
known_pitfalls: [NOTION_UPDATE_ROW_DATABASE] Property payloads are strict; status-like fields may be type select vs status and mismatches commonly trigger HTTP 400 validation errors.
[NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE] Updates must use an existing option name from the schema; unknown labels fail validation.
[NOTION_UPDATE_PAGE] Property names are case-sensitive and must exactly match schema keys; mismatches typically return HTTP 400.
[NOTION_UPDATE_PAGE] Date edits can fail if time_zone is sent alongside timestamps with offsets; omit time_zone or normalize inputs.
[NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE_WITH_FILTER] Queries can return zero results if the database/page is not shared with the integration (even when items exist).
[CLICKUP_UPDATE_TASK] Status must match the list’s allowed label exactly (case/whitespace sensitive); invalid values can fail with HTTP 400 and an ITEM_114-style error.
[CLICKUP_GET_LIST] Status labels are list-scoped; a label that exists elsewhere may still be rejected for the current list.
[CLICKUP_GET_TASKS] Large listings can be truncated/offloaded; design parsing around the structured response (not previews) and iterate pages until completion.
[CLICKUP_GET_TASK_COMMENTS] Comment bodies may be structured and can appear in multiple fields (for example plain text plus nested blocks); parse defensively when validating content.
[CLICKUP_CREATE_TASK_COMMENT] Create response may be metadata-heavy and not echo fully rendered text; store the returned identifier and verify via CLICKUP_GET_TASK_COMMENTS when needed.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Extract each row’s title text and current select/status value without hardcoding property keys
Extract searchable task text from a large task-listing payload for locating a target item before updating.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
def build_task_index(payload):
    results=payload.get('results') or []
    data=(results[0] if results else {}).get('response',{}).get('data',{})
    tasks=data.get('tasks') or []
    out=[]
    for t in tasks:
        blob='\n'.join(str(t.get(k) or '') for k in ('name','description','text_content')).lower()
        out.append((t.get('id'), blob))
    return out
```

NOTION_UPDATE_ROW_DATABASE.description: Updates a specific row/page within a Notion database by its page UUID (row_id). IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION: This action updates INDIVIDUAL ROWS (pages) in a database, NOT the database structure. - To update a ROW/PAGE: Use THIS action with `row_id` (the page UUID) - To update DATABASE SCHEMA (columns, properties, title): Use NOTION_UPDATE_SCHEMA_DATABASE with `database_id` REQUIRED: `row_id` is MANDATORY. This is the UUID of the specific page/row to update. Do NOT pass `database_id` to this action - that parameter does not exist here. Common issues: (1) Use UUID from page URL, not the full URL (2) Ensure page is shared with integration (3) Match property names exactly as in database (4) Use 'status' type for Status properties, not 'select' (5) Retry on 409 Conflict errors (concurrent updates) Supports updating properties, icon, cover, or archiving the row.

icon.description: The emoji to be used as the icon for the page. Must be a single emoji character (e.g., '😻', '🤔'). Empty strings or whitespace-only values are ignored.

cover.description: URL of an external image to be used as the cover for the page (e.g., 'https://google.com/image.png'). Empty strings or whitespace-only values are ignored.

row_id.description: REQUIRED: The page UUID of the database row to update. This is a PAGE ID (not a database ID). A database row in Notion is actually a page - use the page's UUID here. Format: 32-character UUID with hyphens (e.g., '59833787-2cf9-4fdf-8782-e53db20768a5'). NOT a URL or page title. Find this ID in the page URL or via 'Copy link' in Notion. NOTE: To update DATABASE structure/schema, use NOTION_UPDATE_SCHEMA_DATABASE instead. This action only updates individual rows/pages within a database.

delete_row.description: If true, the row (page) will be archived, effectively deleting it from the active view. If the page is already archived, the action will return success with the current page state. If false, the row will be updated with other provided data.

type.description: Type of the property. Common types: title (ONE per database), rich_text, number, select (for dropdowns), multi_select, date, people, files, checkbox, url, email, phone_number, relation. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Use 'select' for dropdown properties - NOT 'status'. The 'status' type is a SPECIAL Notion property type (with 'To-do', 'In progress', 'Complete' groups) that most databases do NOT have. If your property shows a simple dropdown list, use 'select' even if the property is NAMED 'Status'. Read-only/unsupported types (auto-skipped): created_time, created_by, last_edited_time, last_edited_by, formula, rollup, unique_id, place. Title and rich_text values are written as literal plain text and split into Notion rich-text objects when needed.

value.description:
Value formatted according to the property type:
- title, rich_text - literal text string. Values longer than 2,000 UTF-16 units are split across Notion rich-text objects; oversized values fail before writing instead of being truncated.
- number - numeric string ex. "23.4"
- select - single option name (no commas). For multiple values, use multi_select.
- multi_select - comma separated values ex. "India,USA"
- date - ISO 8601. Single: "2021-05-11". Range: "2021-05-11/2021-05-15" (slash-separated).
- people - comma separated USER UUIDs (not names). Use NOTION_LIST_USERS to find UUIDs.
- relation - comma separated PAGE UUIDs (not titles). Use NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE to find UUIDs.
- url - a URL string.
- files - comma separated HTTPS URLs only (no file:// or http://).
- checkbox - "True" or "False"

properties.description: List of properties to update. Each property requires: (1) 'name' - exact property name as shown in Notion, (2) 'type' - the property type (title, rich_text, number, select, status, multi_select, date, people, relation, checkbox, url, email, phone_number, files), (3) 'value' - formatted according to type. IMPORTANT: Verify property names exist in the database and match the exact case. Use 'status' type for Status properties, NOT 'select'. Properties not listed will remain unchanged.

NOTION_CREATE_COMMENT.description: Adds a comment to a Notion page (via `parent_page_id`) OR to an existing discussion thread (via `discussion_id`); cannot create new discussion threads on specific blocks (inline comments).

bold.description: Indicates if the text is bold.

code.description: Indicates if the text is formatted as code.

link.description: URL for hyperlinks or media blocks. For TEXT blocks: optional URL to make text clickable. For MEDIA blocks (image, video, file): REQUIRED - must be a valid external URL (http/https). Do not pass placeholder text in 'content' for media blocks.

color.description: The color of the text background or text itself.

italic.description: Indicates if the text is italic.

content.description: The textual content for TEXT blocks only. ENHANCED: Automatically parses markdown formatting including bold (**text**), italic (*text*), strikethrough (~~text~~), inline code (`code`), and links ([text](url)). Required for: paragraph, heading_1, heading_2, heading_3, callout, to_do, toggle, quote. NOT USED for media blocks (image, video, file) - use 'link' field instead.

underline.description: Indicates if the text is underlined.

strikethrough.description: Indicates if the text has strikethrough.

block_property.description:
The block property of the block to be added. **Common text blocks:** `paragraph`, `heading_1`, `heading_2`, `heading_3`, `callout`, `to_do`, `toggle`, `quote`, `bulleted_list_item`, `numbered_list_item`. **Special blocks:** `divider` (creates a horizontal divider line, no content required). **Media/embed blocks:** `file`, `image`, `video` (requires `link` field with external URL - direct file uploads not supported). 

**NOTE:** Notion API only supports heading levels 1-3. heading_4, heading_5, etc. are automatically converted to heading_3.

comment.description: Content of the comment as a NotionRichText object or a JSON string. Simplest form: {'content': 'Looks good!'} or {'text': 'Looks good!'} (both 'content' and 'text' are accepted as the field name). Can also be passed as a JSON string: '{"content": "Looks good!"}'. Optional styling fields: bold, italic, etc. The 'link' field is for external URLs only (e.g., 'https://example.com'), NOT for page IDs. Do NOT wrap this in a list or use Notion API block JSON.

discussion_id.description: The ID of an existing discussion thread to which the comment will be added. This is required if `parent_page_id` is not provided. Must be a valid UUID (32 hex characters with or without hyphens).

parent_page_id.description: The ID of the Notion page where the comment will be added. This is required if `discussion_id` is not provided. Must be a valid UUID (32 hex characters with or without hyphens). Page IDs can be obtained using other Notion actions that fetch page details or list pages.

CLICKUP_UPDATE_TASK.description: Updates attributes of an existing task; `team_id` is required if `custom_task_ids` is true, use a single space (" ") for `description` to clear it, and provide at least one modifiable field.

parent.description: ID of new parent task to make this a subtask; cannot convert subtask to regular task this way.

status.description: New task status (case-sensitive, must be valid in Workspace).

task_id.description: Unique task identifier; use custom task ID if `custom_task_ids` is true.

team_id.description: Team ID, required if `custom_task_ids` is true.

archived.description: True to archive, false to unarchive.

due_date.description: New due date (Unix timestamp in milliseconds).

start_date.description: New start date (Unix timestamp in milliseconds).

description.description: New task description; use a single space (" ") to clear.

due_date_time.description: True if `due_date` includes time, false if all-day.

assignees__add.description: List of user IDs to add as assignees.

assignees__rem.description: List of user IDs to remove as assignees.

custom_item_id.description: Custom task type ID. Use `1` for Milestone, its ID for custom type. Omit/`None` to make regular task (API's 'null' equivalent).

custom_task_ids.description: If true, `task_id` is a custom ID and `team_id` is required.

start_date_time.description: True if `start_date` includes time, false if all-day.

CLICKUP_CREATE_TASK_COMMENT.description: Adds a comment to a ClickUp task; `team_id` is required if `custom_task_ids` is true.

task_id.description: Unique task identifier for the comment. Can be standard or custom if `custom_task_ids` is true.

team_id.description: Team ID, required if `custom_task_ids` is true to locate the task by its custom ID.

assignee.description: The user ID of the person to whom this specific comment should be assigned or mentioned. This assigns the comment, not the task.

notify_all.description: If `true`, notifications for this comment will be sent to all users watching the task, including the comment's creator. If `false`, notifications will be sent according to standard ClickUp notification rules (e.g., to mentioned users, comment assignee).

comment_text.description: The text content for the comment. Supports ClickUp's comment formatting (e.g., mentions, markdown).

custom_task_ids.description: Set to `true` to indicate that the `task_id` provided is a custom task ID. If `true`, the `team_id` must also be provided.

NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE_WITH_FILTER.description: Tool to query a Notion database with server-side filtering, sorting, and pagination. Use when you need to retrieve a subset of rows by property, date, status, or other conditions.

anyOf.title: PropertySort

property.title: Property
property.description: Name or ID of the database property to sort by. Do NOT use for system timestamps (created_time, last_edited_time) - use TimestampSort instead.

anyOf.description: Sort by a database property name or ID (NOT for system timestamps).

anyOf.title: TimestampSort

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: System timestamp field to sort by. Use 'created_time' for page creation time or 'last_edited_time' for last modification time.

anyOf.description: Sort by a system timestamp field (created or last edited time).

sorts.description: List of sort criteria in order of precedence. Use PropertySort for database properties (with property field) and TimestampSort for system timestamps (with timestamp='created_time' or 'last_edited_time'). IMPORTANT: To sort by page creation or last edited time, you MUST use the TimestampSort format with timestamp='created_time' or timestamp='last_edited_time', NOT property names like 'Created' or 'Last Edited'. Common timestamp field name variations (Created, creation time, Last Edited, etc.) will be automatically converted to the correct format.

filter.description: PREREQUISITE: Call NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE first to discover property names and types. Filter type keys MUST match the property's actual type in the schema. Each filter object MUST contain exactly ONE filter type key. For multiple conditions, use compound filters: {"and": [{"property": "Name", "title": {...}}, {"property": "Description", "rich_text": {...}}]}. 'title' IS A RESERVED PROPERTY NAME: 'title' always refers to the database's built-in primary title column (type 'title', NOT 'select' or 'rich_text'). Even custom properties named 'title' are treated as the built-in title column. FILTER TYPE MUST MATCH SCHEMA TYPE: Property names are NOT reliable indicators of type. A property named 'Status' could be type 'select' in one database but type 'status' in another. 'select' is for dropdowns; 'status' is ONLY for Notion's built-in Status property with workflow groups. SELECT/STATUS/MULTI_SELECT VALUES ARE CASE-SENSITIVE: Option names must match EXACTLY as defined in the database schema, including capitalization and emoji prefixes (e.g., 'Done' not 'done', '✅ Done' not 'Done'). Common mistake: using 'done' when the actual option is 'Done'. Check the database schema for exact option names. Valid filter type keys: title, rich_text, number, checkbox, select, multi_select, status, date, people, files, url, email, phone_number, relation, created_by, created_time, last_edited_by, last_edited_time, formula, unique_id, rollup, verification, timestamp. FORMULA FILTERS: Structure: {'property': '<name>', 'formula': {<result_type>: {<condition>: <value>}}}. Result types: 'string' (rich_text conditions), 'number' (numeric conditions), 'date' (date conditions), 'checkbox' (boolean conditions). The result type MUST match the formula's actual output type. If the formula property value shows type 'boolean', use 'checkbox' in the filter (API naming mismatch). Some complex formulas are unfilterable ('Unable to filter based on a formula of unknown type') - use client-side filtering instead. NOTE: 'text' is NOT valid - use 'rich_text' for text properties or 'title' for title properties. SYSTEM TIMESTAMP FILTERS: Use simplified format: {"created_time": {"on_or_after": "2024-01-01"}} - auto-transformed to correct API format. Filter structure for database properties: {"property": "<property_name>", "<filter_type>": {"<condition>": "<value>"}}. Common conditions by type: title/rich_text: equals, contains, starts_with, ends_with, is_empty, is_not_empty; select/status: equals, does_not_equal, is_empty, is_not_empty; number: equals, does_not_equal, greater_than, less_than, greater_than_or_equal_to, less_than_or_equal_to, is_empty, is_not_empty; checkbox: equals (true/false); date: equals, before, after, on_or_before, on_or_after, is_empty, is_not_empty, past_week, past_month, past_year, next_week, next_month, next_year; relation: contains, does_not_contain (both require a valid page UUID), is_empty, is_not_empty. ROLLUP FILTERS: Require a nested aggregation type wrapper. Do NOT use flat filters like {"rollup": {"contains": "value"}}. Instead use one of: (1) {"rollup": {"any": {<condition>}}} - matches if ANY related item satisfies condition; (2) {"rollup": {"every": {<condition>}}} - matches if ALL related items satisfy condition; (3) {"rollup": {"none": {<condition>}}} - matches if NO related items satisfy condition; (4) {"rollup": {"number": {<number_condition>}}} - for number rollup aggregations (count, sum, avg, etc.); (5) {"rollup": {"date": {<date_condition>}}} - for date rollup aggregations (earliest, latest). Inside rollup.any/every/none, use the filter type matching the underlying property type. Compound filters use 'and' or 'or' arrays: {"and": [<filter1>, <filter2>]} or {"or": [<filter1>, <filter2>]}.

page_size.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–100). Defaults to 100 if omitted.

database_id.description: The UUID of the Notion database to query (32 character hex string, with hyphens or without). IMPORTANT: This must be a DATABASE ID, not a page ID. Page IDs and database IDs are different things. If you have a page URL/ID, that is NOT the same as the database ID - inline databases within pages have their own separate database IDs distinct from the parent page ID. Use NOTION_SEARCH_NOTION_PAGE or NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE to discover the correct database ID. The database must be shared with your integration.

start_cursor.description: Cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor` for fetching the next page. Use the exact cursor value returned by Notion.
